hook: You don't have a short life. You have a wasted one.
body: Two thousand years ago, a Roman philosopher named Seneca noticed something strange.
People guard their money like it's sacred. But they give away their time to anyone who asks.
An hour scrolling. A year in a job you hate. Ten years waiting for the right moment.
And then, at the end, they beg for more time.
Seneca wrote: it is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
Life is long, if you know how to use it.
So ask yourself tonight. Who is spending your time? Because it should be you.

hook: If you never want to get hurt, never love.
body: C. S. Lewis wrote one of the most honest things ever said about love.
To love at all is to be vulnerable. Love anything, and your heart will be broken.
If you want to keep it safe, give it to no one. Lock it away.
And it will not be broken. It will become unbreakable. Impenetrable.
That's the trade most people make after they get hurt. They choose safety.
But a heart that can't be broken also can't be reached.
So if it hurts, it means it was real. Keep it open anyway.

hook: Your life might be pointless. Good.
body: The gods punished Sisyphus with the worst fate they could imagine.
Push a giant boulder up a mountain. Watch it roll back down. Forever.
Albert Camus said that's us. Wake up. Work. Sleep. Repeat.
No grand meaning is coming to rescue you.
But then Camus wrote the most surprising line in philosophy. One must imagine Sisyphus happy.
Because the struggle itself is enough to fill a heart.
The boulder is still there tomorrow. So is the sunrise on the way up.

hook: You didn't fall out of love. You stopped loving.
body: In nineteen fifty six, Erich Fromm wrote a book that changed how people see love.
He said we think love is a feeling. Something that happens to us, like falling.
So when the feeling fades, we think love is gone.
But Fromm said love is an activity. Not falling for someone. Standing in it.
It's care. Responsibility. Respect. Knowing someone, again and again.
Feelings come and go like weather. Love is what you choose to do when they're gone.
So don't ask if you still feel it. Ask if you're still doing it.

hook: Most of your suffering isn't real.
body: Epictetus was born a slave. He had no money, no freedom, and a crippled leg.
And yet he became one of the freest minds in history.
His secret was one sentence. Some things are within our power. Others are not.
Other people's opinions. The past. The weather. Not yours.
Your choices. Your effort. How you respond. Completely yours.
He said we are disturbed not by things, but by our opinions about things.
Stop fighting what you can't hold. Take care of what you can.

hook: The best love doesn't complete you.
body: We grow up believing love means finding our other half.
Someone to fill every empty space. Someone to become one with.
But the poet Rainer Maria Rilke saw it differently.
He wrote that love consists in this. That two solitudes protect, and touch, and greet each other.
Two whole people. Each with their own inner world. Standing next to each other, not inside each other.
Love isn't losing yourself in someone. It's guarding the space where they can be themselves.
Find someone who protects your solitude. And protect theirs.
